domain_entities.name: AuthSession
domain_entities.purpose: Frontend-held authentication state: the bearer token and the signed-in employee's profile, plus the session's lifecycle status. Created on successful login, cleared on logout or on any 401 response.

domain_entities.name: EmployeeProfile
domain_entities.purpose: Read-only view of the signed-in employee shown on the dashboard. Never carries passwordHash or terminationDate.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalanceView
domain_entities.purpose: Read-only leave balance for the signed-in employee, with available computed as entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays (never persisted).

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequestView
domain_entities.purpose: Read-only view of one of the signed-in employee's leave requests, shown in the list and detail views. This feature is read-only: no state transitions are performed by the frontend.

business_rules: All dates returned by the API are rendered in UTC and must never be shifted by the browser's local timezone. A displayed calendar day is derived from the date's UTC components (getUTCFullYear/getUTCMonth/getUTCDate), never local components. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Date rendering (all leave request and balance dates) appears, not only here]

Every authenticated API call after login must send 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. A 401 response on any authenticated call must transition the session to LOGGED_OUT and return the user to the login screen, never render an empty/partial page. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever AuthSession / API client appears, not only here]

Login failure must display the server's error message verbatim and must not reveal whether the email exists. Wrong-password and unknown-email failures are indistinguishable (the API returns identical bodies); the UI must not differentiate them. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Login screen appears, not only here]

available = entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays, computed for display only and never persisted or mutated by the frontend. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalanceView appears, not only here]

The frontend is read-only for leave requests: it may display status but never create, submit, approve, reject, or cancel a request. No state transition is initiated from the UI. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequestView appears, not only here]

The token must be stored on login and cleared on logout and on 401. The signed-in identity is always derived from the stored token/profile, never from a client-supplied id. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever AuthSession appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
This feature is a read-only React web frontend; it introduces no new backend domain concepts and performs no state transitions on existing entities. The domain slice is therefore a set of read-only view entities plus one new client-side session entity.

New entity — AuthSession (lifecycle LOGGED_OUT → LOGGED_IN → EXPIRED → LOGGED_OUT): the frontend-held authentication state. LOGGED_OUT is the initial state; a successful login transitions to LOGGED_IN (token + profile stored); a 401 on any authenticated call transitions to EXPIRED and immediately back to LOGGED_OUT (token cleared, user returned to login); explicit logout transitions LOGGED_IN → LOGGED_OUT. The token is opaque to the domain; the signed-in identity is always derived from the stored token/profile, never a client-supplied id.

Read-only view entities (no lifecycle transitions performed by this feature):
- EmployeeProfile: the signed-in employee's dashboard identity; never carries passwordHash or terminationDate.
- LeaveBalanceView: carries the computed available = entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays (display-only, never persisted). Lifecycle OPEN/CLOSED is inherited from the backend balance concept but is not mutated here.
- LeaveRequestView: one leave request with its full 14-field shape; status lifecycle DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED is displayed but never changed by the frontend.

Binding business rules (broad scope):
- UTC date rendering: all API dates render from UTC components; the browser's local timezone must never shift a displayed day (reintroducing the prior UTC+3 off-by-one defect is forbidden).
- 401 handling: any authenticated call returning 401 forces the session to LOGGED_OUT and returns the user to login, never an empty page.
- Enumeration safety: login failure shows the server's message verbatim and never distinguishes wrong-password from unknown-email.
- available = entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays (display only).
- Read-only leave scope: no create/submit/approve/reject/cancel from the UI.

Open questions (frontend implementation concerns, not domain ambiguities): token storage mechanism (localStorage/sessionStorage/in-memory) and whether to proactively detect JWT expiry vs rely on server 401. Both are deferred to the application architect; the domain model already handles the 401-driven path.

open_questions.question: Where should the bearer token be persisted on the client (localStorage vs sessionStorage vs in-memory)?
open_questions.impact: Affects session persistence across page reloads and XSS exposure surface. The domain model treats the token as opaque state; the storage mechanism is a frontend implementation concern.

open_questions.question: Should the frontend proactively detect token expiry (JWT exp) or rely solely on the server's 401 response?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether the EXPIRED session state is reached by client-side clock inspection or only by a server 401. The domain model already handles 401 → LOGGED_OUT; proactive expiry is optional.
candidate_options: Decode JWT exp client-side and pre-emptively log out
